title: Constitution audit in reviewer/peer-review + session-state registry updates
description:
## Project Context
Judgment laws (constitution laws without check: lines) bind reviewers: this bead adds the per-law audit table to both review surfaces and registers all new .ccu/ files in session-state — the canonical .ccu documentation other skills cite.

## Reasoning / Justification
Reviewers need a FIXED rubric (the constitution) instead of taste; per-law ✓/✗/N/A output makes violations mechanical to route. session-state's ":24 Everything is plain Markdown" framing is now false (gates.json, gate-runs.d) and must be rewritten, not patched around (discovery finding #4).

## Files
- Modify: plugins/agents/reviewer.md (1.3 Review Checklist: constitution audit item; 1.4 Review Output template: new "### Constitution" per-law table section C<n> ✓/✗ file:line/N/A; verdict counts constitution violations as Critical; orchestrator-report line)
- Modify: plugins/commands/t:peer-review.md (new Step 4.5 constitution audit between :34 and :35; Step 7 report includes per-law verdict; skip visibly if no CONSTITUTION.md)
- Modify: plugins/skills/session-state/SKILL.md (files table: add gates.json/CONSTITUTION.md/bin/ /gate-runs.d/ /METRICS.md rows with Written-By; gitignore block: committed vs ignored split per O8; Log Formats: gate-run JSON schema + METRICS.md snapshot template; Initialization: quality-layer pointer to t:init; rewrite the plain-Markdown framing sentence)

## Interfaces

## Considerations

title: Spec-blind verifier: ccu-verify-pack.sh packet builder + verifier agent
description:
## Project Context
The verifier is the epic's information-hiding role (design §Component 3): it confirms each acceptance criterion black-box, from ONLY the bead's spec-side content, so it cannot inherit the coder's assumptions. The packet builder makes that hiding deterministic instead of trusted.

## Reasoning / Justification
Allowlist extraction (not blocklist): anything not explicitly spec-side is dropped, so future bead-template additions can't leak implementation detail by default. A packet leak defeats the entire mechanism — treat exclusion tests as the primary deliverable.

## Files
- Create: plugins/skills/quality-gates/scripts/ccu-verify-pack.sh
- Create: plugins/agents/verifier.md
- Test:   packet exclusion assertions against a synthetic bead carrying ALL sections

## Interfaces
- Consumes: br show <bead-id> --json + br show <epic-id> --json; run_hint from .ccu/gates.json (contract C); .ccu/CONSTITUTION.md format from claude-code-utils-yof (constitution bead)
- Produces: packet file .ccu/artifacts/<epic-dir>/verify-<bead-id>.md — sections: Assignment (title+description), Acceptance Criteria (verbatim), Global Constraints (from epic), Constitution (full text if present), How to Run (run_hint + completion-phase gate commands) — consumed by the verifier agent spawn in the orchestrator-integration bead
- Produces: verifier.md agent contract — model opus; tools Read, Bash, Grep, Glob; final message = per-criterion table PASS / FAIL (repro steps) / UNVERIFIABLE (why)

## Considerations
- ALLOWLIST (include): title, description narrative, ## Acceptance Criteria, epic ## Global Constraints, constitution, run instructions
- EXCLUDE (assert in tests): all bead comments (coder deliverables live there), ## Files, ## Interfaces, ## Technical Notes, ## Reasoning, track-context files, commit hashes, EVIDENCE.md content
- verifier.md hard prohibitions: no git diff/show/log; no br commands (packet is self-contained); no reading .ccu/artifacts/ beyond its own packet; never edits anything
- Verifier drives the app via How to Run; if the app can't start, that's FAIL on all criteria with repro, not UNVERIFIABLE
- Bead descriptions use markdown section headers — extract with awk section-state machine, bash 3.2 clean (O1)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Packet from a synthetic bead containing every section type includes ONLY allowlisted content
      — verify: grep -c '## Files\|## Interfaces\|## Technical Notes\|Deliverables:' packet → 0; acceptance criteria present verbatim
- [ ] Bead comments never appear in packet
      — verify: synthetic bead with br comment "SECRET-MARKER" → grep -c SECRET-MARKER packet → 0
- [ ] Missing constitution → packet notes "no constitution derived" (visible, not silent)
      — verify: grep packet
- [ ] verifier.md contains the prohibition list and the PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIABLE table contract
      — verify: grep for "git diff", "UNVERIFIABLE"

## Technical Notes
- Persona precedent: plugins/agents/reviewer.md structure (frontmatter, workflow, report contract)
- Orchestrator Phase 5.55 spawn + FAIL routing is the orchestrator-integration bead's job — do not edit orchestrator/SKILL.md here

title: Ecosystem detection script for gates.json scaffolding (detect-ecosystem.sh + fixtures)
description:
⚠ HIGH RISK: No ecosystem/project-type detection exists anywhere in this repo — this is genuinely novel capability. Build detect-only with fixtures FIRST; do not wire into bootstrap until detection is proven against real project layouts.

## Project Context
t:init must scaffold a correct .ccu/gates.json for any project type (pnpm/yarn/bun/npm, turbo/nx monorepos, Python, Rust, Go). ccu-gate itself is ecosystem-agnostic; ALL ecosystem knowledge concentrates here so the rest of the layer never assumes npm.

## Reasoning / Justification
Standalone detect-only script (not inline in bootstrap.sh) so it can be tested against fixture dirs in isolation and reused by future skills. Detection is a convenience — output is confirmed by the user and written to editable JSON, so wrong guesses are cheap (design §ecosystem detection).

## Investigate Before Coding
- Read plugins/commands/scripts/t-init/check-tools.sh registry pattern (:33-45) — reuse the pipe-delimited array style for the detection matrix
- Verify packageManager field parsing with jq against a real package.json containing "packageManager": "pnpm@9.1.0"
- Confirm turbo/nx affected-only filter syntax current for the versions in the wild (turbo run lint --filter='...[HEAD]')
- Test fixture dirs under /tmp for each ecosystem before claiming detection works

## Files
- Create: plugins/skills/quality-gates/scripts/detect-ecosystem.sh
- Test:   plugins/skills/quality-gates/scripts/fixtures/ (one minimal dir per ecosystem: npm, pnpm, yarn, bun, turbo, nx, pnpm-workspace, python-uv, python-poetry, rust, go, polyglot, unknown)

## Interfaces
- Consumes: contract C gates.json schema from claude-code-utils-q7s
- Produces: detect-ecosystem.sh <project-root> --json → {ecosystems:["node-pnpm","python-uv",...], monorepo:"turbo"|"nx"|"workspace"|null, gates:[{id,cmd,phase,required}...], diff_ban_sets:["jsts","python",...]} — consumed by the bootstrap --gates bead to write gates.json after user confirmation
- Produces: --human mode listing every detected ecosystem with per-item ✓ (user deselection happens in t:init conversation)

## Considerations
- Priority order (design): packageManager field > lockfiles > ask; monorepo checks BEFORE single-package
- Python: gate included only if tool configured (pytest/ruff/mypy present in pyproject or config file); prefix uv run / poetry run per lockfile
- Go: golangci-lint gate only if .golangci.yml exists
- Polyglot: union of gates + diff-ban sets
- Unknown: emit empty gates with needs_user_input:true — t:init asks for commands verbatim
- bash 3.2 + BSD tools only (O1)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each fixture dir detects its expected ecosystem/monorepo/gates
      — verify: for f in fixtures/*/; do detect-ecosystem.sh "$f" --json | jq -r '.ecosystems[0]'; done → matches fixture names
- [ ] pnpm+turbo fixture produces turbo run commands with affected-only filter on commit-phase gates
      — verify: jq -r '.gates[]|select(.phase=="commit").cmd' → contains "--filter"
- [ ] Polyglot fixture (package.json + pyproject.toml) unions both gate sets and diff_ban_sets
      — verify: jq '.diff_ban_sets|length' → 2
- [ ] Unknown fixture → needs_user_input true, gates empty
      — verify: jq .needs_user_input → true
- [ ] /bin/bash -n clean; no -P grep flags
      — verify: bash -n + grep -c '\-P' script → 0

## Technical Notes
- Detection matrix tables: design.md §Component 1 ecosystem detection (authoritative command lists per ecosystem)
- Fixtures are committed test data — keep each under 5 tiny files

The layer's credibility rests on the gate runner behaving exactly as contracted — selftest is the executable form of contracts A/B plus decisions O1/O4/O5/O8. Dogfooding last, after selftest passes, so a broken layer can't wedge this repo's commits.

title: Implement ccu-gate.sh: commit/full modes, diff bans, constitution checks, remediation output
description:
## Project Context
The gate runner is the spine of the Quality Layer: one deterministic script both the pre-commit hook and bead-completion flow run, replacing prose gate instructions in worker.md/t:auto and the orchestrator's inline smell greps.

## Reasoning / Justification
Two phases (design §Component 1) because full test suites on every commit would make commits painfully slow: --commit runs fast gates + diff bans (<30s target), --full runs everything before a bead closes. Remediation blocks on failure because agents converge dramatically faster when errors carry fix instructions (research finding, design.md).

## Files
- Create: plugins/skills/quality-gates/scripts/ccu-gate.sh
- Modify: plugins/skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md (full gate semantics: modes, SKIP policy O8, justify escape hatch, carve-outs, remediation format, residual --no-verify gap per O7)
- Test:   covered by the selftest bead; this bead hand-verifies against a scratch git repo

## Interfaces
- Consumes: contract A/B/C + lib.sh functions from claude-code-utils-q7s (verbatim)
- Consumes: constitution check grammar (O6): exactly one backtick-wrapped `check: <command>` line per law, single line, extract with ERE from .ccu/CONSTITUTION.md
- Produces: the runnable gate contract every consumer bead cites: ccu-gate --commit / --full --bead <id> / --json, per-gate ✓/✗/SKIP lines + remediation blocks, run-log files per contract B

## Considerations
- Diff scan (O5): added lines only; filter ^+++ headers; --commit uses git diff --cached; guard missing HEAD (first commit) via git rev-parse --verify HEAD || empty-tree hash
- Carve-outs: it.skip/test.skip in a TEST file where test name begins "EXPOSES BUG:" is exempt (tester bug-bounce convention, orchestrator SKILL.md:200); CCU_GATE_JUSTIFY records reason into run log and downgrades diff-ban failure to logged warning — never skips the scan silently
- SKIP policy (O8): skip_if_missing tool absent → SKIP reported + logged, non-blocking; required gate with missing command and NO skip_if_missing → FAIL loud (misconfiguration)
- Constitution gate: laws with check: lines run in both modes, per-law ✓/✗ output; >15 laws → warning "constitution is degrading into a rules file"; missing CONSTITUTION.md → SKIP (constitution not derived yet)
- Remediation block per failed gate id: tests → "fix the implementation, NOT the test; re-run: <cmd>"; lint → "run linter --fix if available"; diff-ban → "remove the suppression and fix the root cause, or set CCU_GATE_JUSTIFY with a reviewable reason"
- Must run correctly with CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT unset and from .ccu/bin/ stable copy resolving lib.sh via SELF_DIR (O4)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] --commit blocks a staged +line matching a suppression pattern with non-zero exit and remediation text
      — verify: scratch repo, stage file adding "// eslint-disable foo", run ccu-gate --commit → exit 1, output contains "CCU_GATE_JUSTIFY"
- [ ] Same commit with CCU_GATE_JUSTIFY="tested manually" → exit 0, run-log file has justify field
      — verify: jq -r .justify <newest gate-run file> → "tested manually"
- [ ] --full --bead X runs completion-phase gates and writes log with bead id
      — verify: jq -r .bead → "X"; jq '.gates|length' → gate count
- [ ] Missing gates.json → exit 3, message contains "t:init"
      — verify: run in bare scratch repo → echo $? → 3
- [ ] Constitution check: seeded failing law reports "✗ C1" and exits 1; law without check: line is ignored by the gate
      — verify: scratch CONSTITUTION.md with one passing + one failing checked law
- [ ] EXPOSES BUG carve-out: staged test file with it.skip("EXPOSES BUG: ...") passes the ban scan
      — verify: exit 0 on that diff
- [ ] First-commit edge: repo with no HEAD → --commit works
      — verify: fresh git init, stage file, run → no crash

## Technical Notes
- ERE only (BSD grep, O1); patterns come from gates.json diff_bans arrays joined with |
- Timing per gate via SECONDS resets (bash 3.2 safe)
- Reference remediation-rich feedback rationale: design.md §Component 1

title: Epic: ccu Quality Layer — deterministic gates, constitution, verifier, risk tiers, metrics
description:
Convert ccu's quality enforcement from prose instructions (probabilistic) into executable artifacts the pipeline runs (deterministic). Five components: gate runner (ccu-gate.sh + .ccu/gates.json + pre-commit hook), project constitution (.ccu/CONSTITUTION.md, max 15 laws), spec-blind verifier (script-assembled packet + new agent role), risk tiers (ccu-risk.sh driving verification depth), and workflow metrics (ccu-metrics.sh + t:metrics).

Design approved 2026-07-13: .ccu/artifacts/2026-07-13-mhr-quality-gate-layer/design.md (decisions D1-D7). Approach with frozen interface contracts A/B/C and synthesis decisions O1-O8: approach.md same dir. Integration points: discovery.md same dir.

## Acceptance Criteria (epic-level)
- [ ] A fresh project can run /t:init and get gates.json, CONSTITUTION.md, .ccu/bin/ stable copies, and a chained pre-commit hook
- [ ] ccu-gate --commit blocks a commit containing a seeded suppression; ccu-gate --full --bead <id> runs all gates and writes a run log
- [ ] Orchestrator verifies beads via gate-run logs, spawns spec-blind verifier for MEDIUM/HIGH-risk beads
- [ ] t:metrics renders 5 metrics from real artifacts
- [ ] selftest.sh passes under /bin/bash (3.2) with CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT unset

## Global Constraints
- Bash 3.2 compatible: no declare -A, no mapfile/readarray, no ${var^^}; BSD grep (ERE only, no -P); sed -i '' on macOS (O1)
- Detection/runner scripts: #!/usr/bin/env bash, set -u (never -e), three output modes (--human/--tsv/--missing) where applicable, help via sed -n '2,12p' "$0" (check-tools.sh conventions)
- jq is the only hard parse dependency; br/bv/ubs degrade with visible per-item "SKIP (reason)" — never silent (O8)
- Quality-layer scripts never modify project source: read, run declared commands, append to .ccu/ only
- Git-committed: .ccu/gates.json, .ccu/CONSTITUTION.md, .ccu/bin/, .ccu/METRICS.md. Gitignored: .ccu/gate-runs.d/ (O2/O8)
- Pre-commit context has NO CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT: .ccu/bin scripts resolve siblings via SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)" (O4)
- Cross-skill references from markdown use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/quality-gates/scripts/...
- ccu-gate exit codes: 0 pass, 1 gate failure, 3 missing gates.json ("run /t:init") — contract A
- Gate run log: one JSON file per run in .ccu/gate-runs.d/<utc-ts>-<pid>.json, schema {ts, mode, bead, gates:[{id,result,seconds,reason?}], justify?} — contract B
- Vietnamese user-facing strings always carry full diacritics
- Conventional commits with "Bead: <id>" footer; no Co-Authored-By trailers

title: t:init quality-layer phase: bootstrap --gates, stable-path copies, pre-commit chain-install
description:
⚠ HIGH RISK: Chain-installing over arbitrary pre-existing git pre-commit hooks can silently break other tooling or double-fire. Prototype the installer against all four states (no hook / existing non-ccu hook / re-apply idempotent / git worktree) in a scratch repo BEFORE touching bootstrap.sh.

## Project Context
Adoption gateway for the whole Quality Layer (design D5): t:init detects and sets up gates.json, constitution, stable script copies, and the pre-commit hook; every workflow then hard-requires the result. Without this bead the layer exists but no project can adopt it.

## Reasoning / Justification
Detection lives in check-state.sh and application in bootstrap.sh because t:init.md explicitly forbids reimplementing detection in the command prompt (t:init.md:26,130) — new capability must follow the split. Stable-path copies in .ccu/bin/ (committed) because git hooks get a bare environment with no CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT and the plugin cache path is volatile (O4, setup-telegram.sh precedent).

## Investigate Before Coding
- Read setup-telegram.sh:105-192 — marker string, stable-path copy, strip-then-re-add idempotent merge; transfer the MECHANISM to a git hook file (different format: plain shell script, not settings.json)
- Prototype: (1) no existing hook → create; (2) existing non-ccu hook → append marker-delimited block, preserve original behavior; (3) re-run → no duplicate block; (4) git worktree → hooks live in the COMMON git dir (git rev-parse --git-common-dir), verify install lands where worktree commits actually trigger it
- Confirm core.hooksPath is respected if set (some repos use husky/lefthook) — if core.hooksPath points elsewhere, install there or warn loudly

## Files
- Modify: plugins/commands/scripts/t-init/check-state.sh (emit gates_json, ccu_bin, constitution, precommit_hook after :73)
- Modify: plugins/commands/scripts/t-init/bootstrap.sh (--gates action: run detect-ecosystem.sh, confirm, write .ccu/gates.json; copy ccu-gate.sh+lib.sh to .ccu/bin/; chain pre-commit; ensure .ccu/gate-runs.d/ gitignored; NEVER gitignore gates.json/.ccu/bin — O8)
- Modify: plugins/commands/t:init.md (quality-layer surfacing in steps 6/8b/10; constitution derivation offer via create-project-rules)
- Test:   scratch-repo matrix run documented in bead comment (4 hook states x worktree)

## Interfaces
- Consumes: detect-ecosystem.sh --json output from claude-code-utils-ens (verbatim schema); NOTE diff_ban_sets are NAMED sets ("jsts","python",...) — bootstrap expands them into concrete diff_bans.suppressions/smells arrays using the commented per-ecosystem pattern blocks in templates/gates.json (claude-code-utils-q7s)
- Consumes: ccu-gate.sh + lib.sh artifacts from claude-code-utils-i04 (files copied to .ccu/bin/)
- Produces: installed hook block — marker "# >>> ccu-gate >>>" ... "# <<< ccu-gate <<<" wrapping: .ccu/bin/ccu-gate.sh --commit || exit 1 (path relative to repo root via git rev-parse) — consumed by every subsequent commit in adopting projects
- Produces: check-state.sh --missing keys gates_json/constitution/precommit_hook — consumed by t:init.md remediation plan

## Considerations
- bootstrap.sh already cd's to git root (:44-45); keep that but use --git-common-dir for the hooks target (worktrees)
- Hook body must check command -v jq >/dev/null || { echo "ccu-gate: jq missing"; exit 1; } — bare env may lack PATH entries (O4)
- Re-running --gates refreshes .ccu/bin/ copies (plugin update propagation)
- --all flag includes --gates; --check never mutates

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Fresh scratch repo: bootstrap --gates creates gates.json (from fixture detection), .ccu/bin/{ccu-gate.sh,lib.sh} executable, chained hook; commit with seeded suppression is BLOCKED
      — verify: git commit exits non-zero, output contains gate name
- [ ] Existing non-ccu pre-commit hook still runs after install
      — verify: hook with echo marker → marker appears before ccu-gate output on commit
- [ ] Re-running bootstrap --gates is idempotent
      — verify: grep -c 'ccu-gate >>>' .git/hooks/pre-commit → 1 after two runs
- [ ] Worktree: commit from a linked worktree triggers the hook
      — verify: git worktree add, seeded suppression commit → blocked
- [ ] check-state.sh --missing lists gates_json when absent, empty when present
      — verify: run before/after bootstrap

## Technical Notes
- Model everything on setup-telegram.sh; hooks are plain shell, so the marker block is textual, not jq
- t:init.md SCRIPT_DIR resolver (:14-24) already handles marketplace installs — new scripts live in the quality-gates SKILL dir, so bootstrap needs its own resolver for them: reuse the find "$HOME/.claude" fallback pattern pointed at skills/quality-gates/scripts

title: ccu-metrics.sh + t:metrics command + t:done/t:opinion/t:next wiring
description:
## Project Context
Closes the measurement loop of the Quality Layer (design §Component 5): five metrics computed from artifacts the layer already produces, so "is the workflow getting better?" has a numeric answer that t:opinion/t:next can cite.

## Reasoning / Justification
Pure read-compute against frozen contract B — buildable against fixture gate-run files before ccu-gate even lands. Churn is a labeled proxy (fix/rework commits touching same files within 14 days) because line-survival blame sampling is expensive; v2 noted in design.

## Files
- Create: plugins/skills/quality-gates/scripts/ccu-metrics.sh
- Create: plugins/commands/t:metrics.md
- Modify: plugins/commands/t:done.md (new step 6.5 after beads sync: run metrics snapshot if quality layer present)
- Modify: plugins/commands/t:opinion.md (add .ccu/METRICS.md to context reads)
- Modify: plugins/commands/t:next.md (add .ccu/METRICS.md to context reads)
- Test:   fixture gate-runs.d dir with 6 synthetic run files

## Interfaces
- Consumes: contract B run-log files from claude-code-utils-q7s (glob .ccu/gate-runs.d/*.json); br list --labels bug --json; git log
- Produces: ccu-metrics.sh [--epic <id>] --json → {first_pass_rate, verification_tax, bug_bounce_rate, suppression_pressure, churn_proxy, window} — consumed by t:metrics.md rendering
- Produces: METRICS.md snapshot format: dated ## section, 5-row table with current value + trend arrow vs previous snapshot (documented in the session-state bead)

## Considerations
- first_pass_rate: % of beads whose FIRST --full run has all gates pass; verification_tax: mean --full runs per bead until first all-pass
- Empty gate-runs.d (fresh project) → every metric renders "n/a (no runs yet)" not 0 — avoid fake zeros (O8 spirit)
- Per-worktree log loss is a documented v1 limitation (O3) — mention in t:metrics.md output caveat
- t:done edit is graceful: skip silently if .ccu/gates.json absent (t:done runs in non-adopted projects too)

## Acceptance Criteria

      — verify: jq output against fixture
- [ ] t:metrics renders 5-row table with trend arrows on second snapshot
      — verify: run twice against fixture, second METRICS.md section has arrows
- [ ] Fresh project → all n/a, exit 0
      — verify: empty dir run
- [ ] t:done contains step 6.5 gated on gates.json presence
      — verify: grep t:done.md

## Technical Notes

title: ccu-risk.sh risk-tier calculator + plan-beads risk reframe
description:
## Project Context
Risk tiers let verification effort land where risk is (design §Component 4): LOW beads flow on gate evidence alone; MEDIUM/HIGH get the spec-blind verifier; HIGH adds security review. This bead builds the calculator and rewrites plan-beads' risk section to use it.

## Reasoning / Justification
Four cheap signals (bv centrality, git hotspots, sensitive keywords, priority) replace judgment-call annotations so plan-beads and orchestrator compute the SAME tier from the same script. IMPORTANT reframe: plan-beads/SKILL.md:125 currently says risk ratings are "annotations, not gates" — that sentence must be REWRITTEN, not appended to: risk now drives verification depth (which verifiers run) while remaining non-blocking guidance for how workers implement.

## Files
- Create: plugins/skills/quality-gates/scripts/ccu-risk.sh
- Modify: plugins/skills/plan-beads/SKILL.md (Phase 2 Risk Classification :123-132 and Risk Indicators :134-149 — replace decision tree with ccu-risk.sh invocation; rewrite the :125 framing; keep the ⚠ HIGH RISK bead-annotation convention; ALSO add the constitution check: Phase 2 synthesis validates the proposed approach against .ccu/CONSTITUTION.md laws before decomposition — a design that violates a law is reworked, not filed. Skip visibly when no CONSTITUTION.md exists)
- Modify: plugins/skills/plan-beads/templates/approach.md (Risk Map intro sentence — same reframe)
- Test:   hand-run against this epic's own beads once filed

## Interfaces
- Consumes: bead JSON via br show <id> --json (## Files paths, description text, priority); bv --robot-triage --graph-root <epic> (centrality, SKIP if bv absent)
- Produces: ccu-risk.sh <bead-id> [--epic <epic-id>] --json → {tier:"LOW"|"MEDIUM"|"HIGH", points:N, reasons:["hotspot: src/auth.ts in top decile", ...]} — consumed by the orchestrator-integration bead (policy table) and plan-beads Phase 2
- Produces: --human mode: tier + per-signal ✓/✗ line each with its reason

## Considerations
- Scoring (design): centrality top-quartile +2; any Files entry in top-10% most-changed over 90 days +2; sensitive keywords (auth,payment,migration,secret,permission,crypto,token,billing) +2; p0/p1 +1. Tiers: 0-1 LOW, 2-3 MEDIUM, >=4 HIGH
- Hotspot computation: git log --since=90.days --name-only | sort | uniq -c — one pass, cache per invocation
- Beads with no ## Files block yet (early planning): hotspot signal reports SKIP, not 0 — visible degradation (O8)
- bash 3.2 (O1); keyword match is case-insensitive ERE on title+description

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] plan-beads Phase 2 contains the constitution-check step with visible-skip wording
      — verify: grep -c 'CONSTITUTION' plugins/skills/plan-beads/SKILL.md → >=1
- [ ] Bead with auth keyword + p1 scores 3 → MEDIUM with two reasons
      — verify: ccu-risk.sh <test-bead> --json | jq -r .tier → MEDIUM
- [ ] bv absent → centrality reason line says SKIP, tier still computed
      — verify: PATH without bv, run → jq .reasons includes "centrality: SKIP"
- [ ] plan-beads SKILL.md no longer contains "not gates" framing; contains ccu-risk.sh invocation
      — verify: grep -c 'annotations, not gates' plugins/skills/plan-beads/SKILL.md → 0; grep -c 'ccu-risk.sh' → >=1
- [ ] Human mode prints per-signal lines
      — verify: ccu-risk.sh <bead> → 4 signal lines each ✓/✗/SKIP

## Technical Notes
- Keep the LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH worker-guidance table in plan-beads (it describes implementation behavior, still valid)
- Tier semantics for orchestration are documented in the orchestrator bead — do not edit orchestrator/SKILL.md here (file ownership: orchestrator-integration bead)

title: Create quality-gates skill foundation: lib.sh, schemas, gates.json template
description:
## Project Context
Foundation bead of the Quality Layer epic: creates the quality-gates skill directory and freezes the three interface contracts (A: ccu-gate CLI, B: gate-run log, C: gates.json schema + stable layout) that every other bead in this epic compiles against. Get this right first — churn here ripples everywhere.

## Reasoning / Justification
One skill owns all quality-layer executables (design D6) so contracts stay versioned together. Per-run log files instead of appended JSONL (O2) because parallel workers + no flock on macOS make appends unsafe; one JSON object per file is atomic by construction.

## Files
- Create: plugins/skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md (skeleton: purpose, the three contracts verbatim, script inventory; full gate semantics doc added by the ccu-gate bead)
- Create: plugins/skills/quality-gates/scripts/lib.sh
- Create: plugins/skills/quality-gates/templates/gates.json
- Test:   manual — bash -n lib.sh under /bin/bash; jq . templates/gates.json

## Interfaces
- Produces: contract A — ccu-gate CLI: modes --commit | --full --bead <id>; flag --json; env CCU_GATE_JUSTIFY="<reason>"; exit 0 pass / 1 gate failure / 3 missing gates.json (message: run /t:init)
- Produces: contract B — run log: .ccu/gate-runs.d/<utc-ts>-<pid>.json, one JSON object: {ts, mode, bead, gates:[{id, result:"pass"|"fail"|"skip", seconds, reason?}], justify?}
- Produces: contract C — gates.json v1: {version:1, gates:[{id, cmd, phase:"commit"|"completion", required, skip_if_missing?}], diff_bans:{suppressions[], smells[]}, run_hint}; stable layout .ccu/bin/{ccu-gate.sh,lib.sh} committed
- Produces: O6 constitution check grammar, stated in SKILL.md skeleton: exactly one backtick-wrapped `check: <command>` line per law, single line, ERE-extractable, exit 0 = compliant — consumed by claude-code-utils-yof (template) and the ccu-gate parser
- Produces: lib.sh functions — gates_json_path() (git rev-parse --show-toplevel based, O3), parse_gates(<phase>) (TSV lines: id<TAB>cmd<TAB>required<TAB>skip_if_missing via jq -r), log_run_begin/log_run_end (contract B writer), fmt_result(<id> <pass|fail|skip> [reason]) (aligned ✓/✗/SKIP line), die_no_config() (exit 3 + run /t:init message)
- Consumes: nothing — this is the root bead

## Considerations
- Bash 3.2: represent parsed gates as jq-produced TSV lines iterated with while IFS=$'\t' read — no associative arrays (O1)
- lib.sh must be sourceable with CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT unset (O4) — no plugin-root references anywhere in it
- gates.json template ships the JS/TS example from design.md §Component 1 plus commented per-ecosystem diff-ban pattern sets (JS/TS, Python, Rust, Go) for the scaffolder to select from
- Worktrees resolve .ccu at the worktree root; committed artifacts exist per-checkout automatically; gate logs are per-worktree — documented v1 limitation (O3)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] lib.sh parses templates/gates.json into phase-filtered TSV gate lines
      — verify: bash -c 'source plugins/skills/quality-gates/scripts/lib.sh; parse_gates commit < plugins/skills/quality-gates/templates/gates.json' → lint/typecheck/ubs lines, no test/build
- [ ] log writer produces a file matching contract B
      — verify: write one run in a temp dir, jq -e '.ts and .mode and (.gates|type=="array")' <file> → true
- [ ] Missing gates.json path → exit 3 with message containing "t:init"
      — verify: cd into tmp git repo without .ccu, source lib.sh, call die-path → echo $? → 3
- [ ] O6 check grammar stated in SKILL.md
      — verify: grep -c 'check: <command>' plugins/skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md → >=1
- [ ] All three contracts stated verbatim in SKILL.md
      — verify: grep -c 'gate-runs.d' plugins/skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md → >=1; grep exit-code table present
- [ ] bash 3.2 clean — verify: /bin/bash -n scripts/lib.sh → no output; no declare -A/mapfile in file

## Technical Notes

- Full schema rationale: .ccu/artifacts/2026-07-13-mhr-quality-gate-layer/approach.md (contracts section + O1-O4)

title: DCG pattern: block git commit --no-verify (hook-bypass hardening)
description:
## Project Context
The pre-commit hook is the Quality Layer's deterministic boundary — but git commit --no-verify (-n) skips hooks entirely, dropping enforcement back to probabilistic. Promoted from optional to in-scope (decision O7): ship a DCG pattern blocking it for agents in DCG-guarded environments.

## Reasoning / Justification
DCG is whitelist-first with modular packs and already blocks destructive git commands — a bypass-block pattern is its natural home. Residual gaps (merge commits, environments without DCG) are documented honestly in quality-gates SKILL.md by the ccu-gate bead; the orchestrated-flow backstop is Phase 5.5 gate-log verification.

## Investigate Before Coding
- Locate DCG's pattern/pack configuration: read the dcg skill (plugins/skills/dcg/SKILL.md) for how user-level patterns or packs are added; determine whether ccu can ship a pattern declaratively or must document a one-line user setup in t:init
- Verify the pattern matches both --no-verify and -n forms of git commit without false-positives on e.g. "git commit -m 'no-verify mentioned'"
- Confirm behavior when DCG is not installed: t:init should surface "hook-bypass guard: SKIP (dcg not installed)" — visible degradation (O8)

## Files
- Modify: plugins/skills/dcg/SKILL.md (document the bypass-block pattern and its install location; record the final pattern-location decision in a bead comment before implementing)
- Modify: plugins/commands/scripts/t-init/check-state.sh (emit dcg bypass-guard status) — coordinate: this file is also touched by claude-code-utils-nvw; this bead lands AFTER it (sequenced via epic track, no code conflict: separate emit lines)
- Test:   dcg dry-run: the pattern blocks "git commit --no-verify -m x" and "git commit -n -m x", allows "git commit -m 'uses --no-verify flag docs'"

## Interfaces
- Consumes: installed pre-commit hook from claude-code-utils-nvw (the thing being protected)
- Produces: bypass-block pattern + t:init SKIP-visible status line

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] dcg blocks both bypass forms in a guarded shell
      — verify: dcg test/dry-run output for the two commands → blocked
- [ ] Message tells the agent WHY and what to do instead
      — verify: block message mentions ccu-gate and fixing the failure
- [ ] Commit-message false-positive is allowed
      — verify: dry-run on quoted string form → allowed
- [ ] t:init shows the guard status per-item
      — verify: check-state --human contains bypass-guard row

title: CONSTITUTION.md template + create-project-rules promotion step
description:
## Project Context
The constitution is the tiny set of absolute laws (max 15) that gates check mechanically and reviewers audit per-law (design §Component 2). This bead ships the template and teaches create-project-rules to derive it from its generated rules.

## Reasoning / Justification
Derivation beats authorship: create-project-rules already produces tailored rules; promoting the few ABSOLUTE ones (would always block a merge, never context-dependent) keeps the constitution honest. Checked laws execute shell on every commit — the template must say so plainly (O6 foot-gun).

## Files
- Create: plugins/skills/quality-gates/templates/CONSTITUTION.md
- Modify: plugins/skills/create-project-rules/SKILL.md (new promotion step at end of "Writing the rules" :124-141, chained before the offer-to-commit line)
- Test:   template's example checked laws run green against a scratch dir

## Interfaces
- Consumes: check grammar from contract docs (claude-code-utils-q7s SKILL.md): exactly one backtick-wrapped `check: <command>` line per law, single line, ERE-extractable; exit 0 = compliant
- Produces: .ccu/CONSTITUTION.md structure — header warning comment, three ## groups (Architecture / Data & Security / Process), laws as "- **C<n>.** <one line>" optionally followed by an indented check line — consumed by ccu-gate (claude-code-utils-i04), the verifier packet builder, and the reviewer-audit bead
- Produces: create-project-rules promotion flow — select candidates, confirm list with user via AskUserQuestion, write file, remind that check bodies are executable code requiring review

## Considerations
- Template header comment MUST state: laws are absolute; check bodies are shell-executed on every commit — review them like code (O6)
- Boundary sentence in header: CLAUDE.md = how we write code (conventions); constitution = what must never happen (laws)
- Example laws in template: one greppable architecture law, one secrets-pattern law (Data & Security), one process law without check: — showing both kinds
- Promotion criteria in SKILL.md edit: absolute (always blocks), mechanical where possible, max 15, when unsure DEMOTE to CLAUDE.md

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Template parses under the O6 grammar: every check line extractable with one ERE
      — verify: grep -E '`check: [^`]+`' templates/CONSTITUTION.md count == number of checked example laws
- [ ] Template's example checks execute (exit 0) in a compliant scratch dir
      — verify: extract + run each → all 0
- [ ] create-project-rules SKILL.md contains promotion step with the executable-code warning and the max-15 rule
      — verify: grep for "promote", "15", "executed"
- [ ] Vietnamese-diacritics example law included (project convention from user CLAUDE.md)
      — verify: template contains a diacritics law example

## Technical Notes

- The reviewer/peer-review audit-table consumers are a separate bead — do not edit those files here
